rationale: Start with a broad, mid-temperature scouting gradient to maximize the chance all 10 compounds elute within 42 min while giving a first map of the elution window and any critical adjacent pairs. This should reveal whether the useful phi range is much narrower and whether later runs should focus on slope or temperature changes.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only available gain is reducing t_last; the first move should be a shorter gradient at the same window and temperature to see how much time can be shaved before the closest cluster around peaks 5–7 starts to lose resolution. Keeping phi0, phi1, and T fixed isolates slope effects cleanly.

The 16 min run is nearly optimal already, but the worst pair is still just above the 1.5 threshold, so one more small reduction in tG is the fastest way to test whether we can pull t_last under 10 min without sacrificing full resolution. This is the clean next step on the same axis before changing temperature or the phi window.

The limiting pair (6,7) lost too much resolution when the gradient was shortened, and pairs with nearly equal slope often respond better to temperature than to further slope changes. Holding the fast 14 min gradient and raising T tests whether selectivity can recover enough to get that pair back to at least 1.5 while keeping t_last under 10 min.

The critical pair is highly temperature-sensitive and worsened badly at 45 C, so the best chance to improve on injection 2 is to move temperature in the opposite direction while keeping the proven 16 min gradient. Lowering T may increase selectivity for peaks 6/7 enough to keep all pairs at baseline resolution, even if t_last rises slightly.

The 16 min, 40 C method is close to optimal, so now trim the gradient window to the actual elution window to spend gradient where the peaks are and potentially improve the crowded middle cluster without lengthening the run. Based on the prior run, all peaks elute roughly within phi_e ~0.13–0.39, so 0.10–0.80 is still safely broad while much less steep than 0.05–0.95.

The narrowed window did not help because it mainly delayed the run, while the key uncertainty remains whether a small temperature increase can push the 16 min method below 10 min without destroying the critical mid-cluster. Testing 45 C at the proven 16 min broad-window method directly probes that tradeoff.

The best method is still 16 min at 40 C, and temperature changes hurt selectivity, so the next lever is a gentler reduction of gradient range rather than a big window trim. Lowering only phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 should slightly shallow the gradient and may boost the critical 6/7 resolution while keeping the last peak close to 10 min.

At phi1 0.90 and 16 min, the critical pair regained comfortable resolution, suggesting room to shorten tG while keeping the gentler slope than the 0.95 window. This tests whether a 14 min gradient with the slightly reduced phi1 can retain full resolution and bring t_last back under 10 min.

Injection 9 is very close to ideal: only the 6/7 pair is slightly below full credit while t_last is already under 10 min. Dropping phi1 one more step should modestly flatten the gradient and improve that pair’s resolution, with a good chance of keeping the last peak at or just under 10 min.

The 0.90/14/40 method is currently best but misses full credit only on pair 6/7, while the 0.85/14/40 method fixes resolution at the cost of pushing t_last above 10 min. A 5 C drop at phi1 0.90 may nudge selectivity for the critical pair upward enough to reach full resolution while keeping the time penalty smaller than at phi1 0.85.

The best region is clearly around 14 min at 40 C, and lowering phi1 improves the critical 6/7 pair; the remaining question is whether a shorter gradient with the flatter 0.85 window can preserve full resolution while clawing back the small time penalty. This is the key exploitation test for a possible score above 0.989.

Changing phi1 from 0.90 to 0.85 trades time for resolution, so the most plausible path to a score above 0.989 is a small temperature increase at the best 0.90/14 condition to trim t_last while hoping the critical pair stays closer to its current behavior than it did at the steeper 0.95 window. This directly tests whether the gentler 0.90 slope buffers the selectivity loss seen at 45 C.

Temperature clearly shifts the critical selectivity strongly, and the unresolved question is whether at the flatter 0.85 window that shift might shorten the run enough while preserving acceptable 6/7 resolution. This is a targeted test around the only two near-optimal settings found so far: 0.90/14/40 for time and 0.85/14/40 for resolution.

Since 45 C consistently shortens retention but damages the critical pair, the only chance it helps is with a shallower gradient that may restore enough 6/7 resolution. Testing 0.85/16/45 checks whether added gradient time can offset the temperature-driven selectivity loss while keeping the last peak near 10 min.

We have bracketed the optimum mainly with phi1 and tG, but have not tested whether a modest increase in phi0 can speed the late peak without harming the critical 6/7 pair at the best 0.90/14/40 setting. The first peak is still well retained, so raising phi0 to 0.10 is a safe way to probe whether the useful window can be shifted upward for a small net gain.

Injection 16 is the new best and is only slightly short of full credit on pair 6/7, so the next local move is to lower phi1 one step while keeping the improved higher phi0. That should flatten the gradient just enough to try to push 6/7 to at least 1.5, and with t_last already only 9.50 min there is room for a modest delay.

Now that full score has been reached, the only useful remaining objective is to find the shortest method that still keeps every pair at or above 1.5 and t_last at or below 10 min. Reducing tG by one step from the successful 0.10/0.85/14/40 method is the cleanest test of whether the optimum is robust or exactly on the edge.

Since shortening tG broke the critical pair, the remaining way to search for a faster equally perfect method is to shift the whole gradient window upward while keeping the successful slope and temperature. Raising phi0 from 0.10 to 0.15 may reduce overall retention, especially for the late peak, while preserving the shallower 0.75 window that resolved 6/7.

Injection 19 shows that shifting the window upward improved both speed and the critical 6/7 resolution while retaining a perfect score, so one more step up in phi0 is the logical exploitation move. This tests whether we can further shorten the method without pushing the first peak into the unretained region or collapsing the key pair.

phi0 = 0.20 pushed the critical 6/7 pair back below full credit, so stay with the successful phi0 = 0.15 and now lower phi1 one step to flatten the slope slightly while keeping the improved speed from the upward-shifted window. This has a good chance to preserve the perfect score and may offer a more robust optimum than 0.15/0.85/14/40.

We already have multiple perfect methods, so the remaining value is to probe whether a compensating temperature decrease can rescue the 12 min gradient that otherwise loses the 6/7 pair. Testing 0.15/0.85/12 at 35 C directly asks whether stronger low-temperature selectivity can deliver a shorter perfect method than the current 14 min optimum.

The 12 min method at lower temperature failed by changing the critical selectivity to a 5/6 problem, so the complementary unexplored edge case is a higher temperature at the same fast gradient. This tests whether the temperature shift can instead favor the crowded cluster enough to preserve baseline resolution in a shorter run, even though prior 45 C runs were generally risky.

With only two injections left and two perfect methods already found, the remaining useful search is a neighboring condition that might also score 1.000 while improving robustness or trimming runtime. Combining the better-resolved lower phi0 branch with the flatter phi1 = 0.80 slope tests a previously untried local variant around the proven optimum zone.

For the final shot, probe the only untested immediate neighbor of the perfect 0.15/0.85/14/40 method: raising phi1 one step while keeping the successful higher phi0. This could retain full resolution and slightly accelerate the late peak enough to give another perfect, potentially more time-efficient optimum.
